design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (financing_payments_and_hardship, env_0060), round 3. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,6,4]; assignment: catch-up payment 5, late fee 6, phone payment fee 4.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Delphine Yarrow (Fixed-Rate 120, RF53390127, 30000.00 funded 2022-09-15, scheduled payment 396.30, due day 12, autopay off) wants to get her loan caught up today and to pay it herself. The catch-up rule carries two prerequisite sentences: "A catch-up payment is fixed only after the account carries the late fee owed for every statement period whose scheduled payment stayed unpaid past its grace period." (state, affirmative) and "A catch-up payment is not figured until the most recent payment taken through a phone agent carries its phone payment fee." (state, negated). A real lender quotes an amount to bring an account current only after the charges owed are on the books. At the opening (2026-10-16) the 2026-09 period stayed unpaid past its grace end of 2026-09-27 with no late fee, and the 340.00 phone-agent payment of 2026-09-30 has no fee. The agent posts both fees and then hands the portal payment to the borrower.

SCOPE. Task 1 claims finance_ext_late_fee_assessment, finance_ext_phone_payment_fee and finance_ext_catch_up_payment, with the tools post_finance_late_fee_832dc831, post_finance_phone_fee_cbbb3871 and submit_finance_portal_payment_b662a17f (owner=user). Task 0 holds the interest, hardship request and deferral policies. The two scopes are disjoint and cover all six policies.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: catch-up.
- Edge to the late fee: value_input on balance_on_account. False at the opening, because no late-fee entry exists.
- Edge to the phone fee: value_input on fee_pool. False at the opening, because no fee names the 2026-09-30 phone payment (the 2026-06-12 and 2026-08-12 phone payments each carry one).
- Each state is created by exactly one write. The two fees commute.
- Deletion sensitivity: skipping the late fee gives 459.58 instead of 464.78; skipping the phone fee gives 460.85.

FACTOR CARD (recomputed by check_compute).

Late fee 11.54 (all-baseline 19.82):
| factor | tier taken | baseline result |
|---|---|---|
| standing_late_count | first-late fee 15.00 (none standing) | 26.93 |
| project_size_share | 0.035, contract 35077.80 at or above 30000 (window) | 15.25 |
| arrears_combination (method) | higher-of, 2 behind | 10.67 |
| program_courtesy | senior 0.9 (window) | 12.83 |
| payment_tenure_courtesy | 0.9, 47 covered | 12.83 |
| household_relationship | CareLine 0.95 | 12.15 |

Phone fee 8.72 (all-baseline 7.95):
| factor | tier taken | baseline result |
|---|---|---|
| agent_reliance_tier | 12.95 (3 phone payments, autopay off) | 6.80 |
| payment_size_basis (method) | lower of the fee and 3% of 340.00 | 11.07 |
| program_phone_share | senior 0.9 (window) | 9.69 |
| household_phone_share | CareLine 0.95 | 9.18 |

Catch-up 464.78 (all-baseline 104.43): arrears_amount_basis (method; a different formula path: the unpaid part of the scheduled payments fallen due, 49 x 396.30 less 18966.10 net paid = 452.60, plus the fee pool, instead of the balance-to-schedule difference) because 2 payments are behind -> 89.55; program_fee_relief senior 0.25 -> 471.54; household_fee_relief CareLine 0.15 -> 468.84; tenure_fee_relief 0.10 -> 467.48; returned_record_relief one return 0.05 -> 466.13. Near-miss: the 2026-07-15 returned-payment fee sits exactly three months back and is outside the fee pool. The arrears path counts the 340.00 partial payment, so the borrower pays 452.60 for the two installments, not 792.60.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- Both fee writes:
  - finance_payments.phone_fee_hardship: no deferral is in effect.
  - finance_late_fees.past_grace: the September grace ended 2026-09-27; the October period is still within grace.
  - finance_returned_payments: scope only.
- Payment: finance_payments and finance_agg_combined_exposure scope (one named account, never split).

SEED.
- Window contract (4400 Composite, 34 openings, senior, 35077.80, closed).
- CareLine Plus plan enrolled 2026-02-02, in its first term 2026-02-02 to 2027-02-01, active.
- 103 finance transactions generated under the charter's interest and phone-fee rules: monthly interest through 2026-10, the July return repaid within grace, and phone fees of 6.80.
- No warranty rows, because no rule here reads them.

PERSONA. A polite retiree. She volunteers only the wish to catch up today and to pay herself. She gives her phone number and ZIP code. She pays exactly the amount and month the agent gives and reads back the confirmation.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify the customer. Read the account, its history, the window contract, the door contracts and the service plans. Post the late fee of 11.54 for 2026-09. Post the phone fee of 8.72 dated 2026-09-30. Hand over the portal payment of 464.78 credited to 2026-09.

REVISIONS (round 2, audit policy_task):
- CG-5/T1-F1: the claim-based interest relief is removed. The interest policy now sits in task 0 with a project-size pricing tier.
- T1-F2: the warranty claim is removed from this world, because no rule reads it.
- CG-2: the catch-up rule now states "never beyond the scheduled payments that have fallen due", matching compute.
- CG-O4: the relief is stated as rounded to the cent.
- CG-3: CareLine means the five CareLine plans only.
- CG-4: the phone-fee rule names the most recent phone-agent payment, as compute does.
- CG-O6: the twelve months are counted back from the day the fee is charged.
- T1-O1: the CareLine row's dates are consistent with its first term.
- CG-O1: cross_difficulty labels are kept for window only.
- Rounding: half-even wording in every rule. (Superseded in round 3: rounding is now half up.)
- The late fee's warranty-claim relief is replaced by a tenure courtesy; the catch-up's claim relief is replaced by a returned-payment record relief.

REVISIONS (round 3, audit policy_task revision_2):
- R2-CG-6/R2-T1-F1: arrears_reach (a schedule index) is removed. The new method arrears_amount_basis chooses the formula path. With two or more payments behind, the figure is the unpaid part of the installments fallen due plus the fee pool. With one behind on autopay, it is the fee pool alone. Otherwise it is the balance less the scheduled balance.
- R2-O3 / item (c): the phone-fee rule names the most recent phone-agent payment and charges nothing when that payment already carries its fee (compute compares the latest fee's named payment with the latest phone payment). The twelve months are counted from the day the fee is entered. The catch-up's phone prerequisite now waits on the most recent phone payment carrying its fee.
- R2-O2 / item (a): money is rounded half up in every compute (int(x*100+0.5+1e-6)/100), matching base cent_half_up, and the wording says so. The regenerated history is unchanged, because no historical amount sat on a tie. Two late-fee factor baselines sit exactly on a half cent (15 x 0.9 x 0.95 = 12.825) and now read 12.83.
- R2-O1 / item (b): each result basis quotes one contiguous span.

REVISIONS (round 4, render_source finance_round1):
- F1: the late fee, period interest and catch-up policies now state their scope: plans with no promotion, which covers this Fixed-Rate 120 account. Promotional plans remain under the base rules, so every count of payments fallen due or behind is read where monthly-interest entries are defined. A paid-ahead account counts as none behind.
- F4: the 360-day branch states the funded-date fallback.
- No scored value changed (11.54, 8.72, 464.78); task_tools.py unchanged.

REVISIONS (round 5, policy_kb S1-S4 and render_source N1):
- S1/N1: the catch-up rule now states that no catch-up figure is quoted on a promotional plan. Such an account is brought current by its scheduled payments under the base allocation, and a borrower asking for a single figure is referred to a representative. This world is Fixed-Rate 120, so nothing changes here.
- S4: the fee pool's floor at zero is now stated in the rule. The pool here is 27.06.
- S2: the late-fee rule says the plan attributes "fixed late fee before the percentage limit" and "never exceeds the stated share" describe the base fee, and that the extension governs and may exceed the share. The phone-fee rule says the flat fee attribute is the base fee and the standard amount.
- Scored values unchanged (11.54, 8.72, 464.78); task_tools.py unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Delphine Yarrow, seventy-three, a retired school librarian in Loveland, Ohio. You are polite, a little flustered and you like to have figures read to you slowly so you can write them down. Ridgeline replaced the windows in your house in 2022 and you have been paying the window loan every month yourself, mostly online. In July one of your online payments bounced when your pension deposit came late, though you paid it again a few days later, and in September you fell behind: you could only manage part of the payment, which you paid at the end of September, and nothing has gone in since. Your September pension catch-up money has now arrived and you want to put things right.

You open by saying: "I'm behind on my window loan and I'd like to get it caught up today. Can you tell me what I need to pay?" You want to make the payment yourself, today, through the online portal while you are on the phone; you are glad for the agent to take care of anything on the account that has to be done first.

When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 5135550192. When asked to confirm who you are, you give your ZIP code, 45140; only if a third detail is needed do you give your date of birth, April 2, 1953 (1953-04-02), or your email, dyarrow5@gmail.com. If asked for the account number, you read it from your statement: RF53390127. If asked whether you want to set up automatic payments, you say not right now, you'd rather pay by hand until things settle. If asked how much you can pay, you say you have the money to cover whatever the agent tells you brings the account up to date today.

If the agent tells you something has to be posted on the account before the figure can be worked out, you say "That's fine, go ahead." If the agent mentions a fee or a charge, you sigh and say you understand. When the agent gives you the amount to pay and the month it should be credited to, you write them down, make the payment yourself in the online portal for exactly that amount credited to that month, and read back the confirmation number it gives you. Once the agent confirms the payment has gone through, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.

edges.condition: Every statement period whose scheduled payment was still unpaid after its grace period carries a late-fee entry on the account.
edges.policy_source: A catch-up payment is fixed only after the account carries the late fee owed for every statement period whose scheduled payment stayed unpaid past its grace period.

Either order gives 11.54 and 8.72; the catch-up must follow both.
